page: Amazon Web Services c9g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz on the arm64 architecture, without multithreading. Cache resources consist of 64 KB L1 instruction and data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 96 MB L3 cache. The instance is outfitted with 384.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include ARM AES cryptographic instruction support, while x86-specific extensions like AVX and AMX are absent. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, and no local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs are included in the configuration.

Benchmark results highlight exceptionally high multi-core scaling and memory throughput. Multi-core performance tests such as stress-ng and PassMark CPU score reach top-tier rankings, supported by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 1910.26 GB/sec and static web serving throughput of 341.63 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth reaches 729.09 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside Redis SET performance of 511.16 million operations per second. While prompt processing for small and medium language models scores within the upper tiers, single-core processing scores in average bands and LLM text generation rates remain low due to CPU-bound sequential processing limitations.

The high physical core count and high memory bandwidth deliver favorable compute density per instance, providing strong efficiency for highly parallelized workloads without paying for unused GPU or bundled storage components. However, reliance on network-attached storage is mandatory, and applications dependent on x86 vector extensions or high per-core single-thread clock rates may encounter performance tradeoffs. Optimal workloads include highly parallel CPU computing, large-scale Redis in-memory caching, web serving clusters, batch data decompression, software compilation, and enterprise database operations.
